questions.q: Which of the following can thermodynamics NOT tell us about a reaction?
questions.sol: Thermodynamics looks only at initial and final states. Rate and mechanism belong to chemical kinetics.
o: The rate at which it proceeds
The extent to which it proceeds

questions.q: The laws of thermodynamics are applicable to:
questions.sol: NCERT stresses that thermodynamics deals with macroscopic (bulk) systems, not microscopic ones.
o: Macroscopic systems with a very large number of molecules

questions.q: Thermodynamics deals with:
questions.sol: NCERT 5.1: thermodynamics is concerned with energy changes of a system as a whole (macroscopic properties). Its laws deal with energy changes of macroscopic systems involving a large number of molecules, not microscopic ones; they do not depend on the structure of atoms or molecules, and they tell nothing about how fast a change happens (that is chemical kinetics). They tell whether, under given conditions, a change is possible and what energy is involved.
questions.hint: "Whether" and "how much", not "how fast".
o: the rate at which a reaction proceeds and its mechanism
energy changes in macroscopic systems, without needing to know the molecular or atomic structure or the time taken
the motion of individual molecules only

hi.q: ऊष्मागतिकी का संबंध है:
o: अभिक्रिया की गति तथा उसकी क्रियाविधि से
स्थूल निकायों में ऊर्जा परिवर्तनों से, बिना आण्विक या परमाण्विक संरचना या लगने वाले समय को जाने
केवल अलग-अलग अणुओं की गति से
hi.sol: NCERT 5.1: ऊष्मागतिकी पूरे निकाय (स्थूल गुणों) के ऊर्जा परिवर्तनों से संबंधित है। इसके नियम बड़ी संख्या में अणुओं वाले स्थूल निकायों के ऊर्जा परिवर्तनों से संबंधित हैं, सूक्ष्म निकायों से नहीं; ये परमाणुओं या अणुओं की संरचना पर निर्भर नहीं करते, और परिवर्तन कितनी तेज़ी से होता है यह नहीं बताते (वह रासायनिक बलगतिकी है)। ये बताते हैं कि दी गई परिस्थितियों में परिवर्तन संभव है या नहीं और उसमें कितनी ऊर्जा लगती है।
hi.hint: "होगा या नहीं" और "कितना", "कितनी तेज़ी से" नहीं।

questions.q: A reaction is carried out in a beaker. The system, surroundings and boundary are respectively:
questions.sol: NCERT 5.1.1: the system is the part of the universe in which observations are made, here the reaction mixture. The rest of the universe is the surroundings: the beaker, the air, the room. The universe = system + surroundings. The wall that separates the system from the surroundings is the boundary; it may be real or imaginary, and it lets us control and keep track of the matter and energy exchanged.
questions.hint: System = what you study.
o: the beaker; the reacting mixture; the air
the whole universe; the beaker; the reacting mixture
the reaction mixture; everything else (the beaker, the air, the room); the wall that separates them, real or imaginary
the air in the room; the reacting mixture; the beaker

hi.q: एक अभिक्रिया बीकर में की जाती है। निकाय, परिवेश तथा परिसीमा क्रमशः हैं:
o: अभिक्रिया मिश्रण; शेष सब कुछ (बीकर, वायु, कमरा); उन्हें अलग करने वाली दीवार, वास्तविक या काल्पनिक
कमरे की वायु; अभिक्रिया मिश्रण; बीकर
hi.sol: NCERT 5.1.1: निकाय ब्रह्मांड का वह भाग है जिसमें प्रेक्षण किए जाते हैं, यहाँ अभिक्रिया मिश्रण। ब्रह्मांड का शेष भाग परिवेश है: बीकर, वायु, कमरा। ब्रह्मांड = निकाय + परिवेश। निकाय को परिवेश से अलग करने वाली दीवार परिसीमा है; यह वास्तविक या काल्पनिक हो सकती है, और इससे हम द्रव्य तथा ऊर्जा के आदान-प्रदान को नियंत्रित तथा दर्ज कर पाते हैं।
hi.hint: निकाय = जिसका अध्ययन करें।

questions.q: For practical purposes in thermodynamics, the surroundings are:
questions.sol: Formally the surroundings are everything except the system, but in practice only the region that can interact with the system matters.
o: The entire universe except the system
That portion of the rest of the universe which can interact with the system

questions.q: Which statement about the boundary of a thermodynamic system is correct?
questions.sol: The boundary can be a real wall (beaker) or an imaginary surface defined by coordinates.
o: It must always be a physical wall
It can be real or imaginary
It never allows energy to pass
It is part of the surroundings only

questions.q: Match the system with its type: (a) reactants in an open beaker; (b) reactants in a closed vessel of conducting material such as copper; (c) reactants in a thermos flask (insulated closed vessel). (i) isolated; (ii) open; (iii) closed.
questions.sol: NCERT 5.1.2: an open system exchanges both energy and matter with the surroundings (open beaker). A closed system exchanges energy but not matter (closed copper or steel vessel). An isolated system exchanges neither energy nor matter (thermos flask or any closed insulated vessel).
questions.hint: Matter + energy → open; energy only → closed; nothing → isolated.

hi.q: निकाय का उसके प्रकार से मिलान कीजिए: (a) खुले बीकर में अभिकारक; (b) कॉपर जैसे चालक पदार्थ के बंद पात्र में अभिकारक; (c) थर्मस फ्लास्क (विलगित बंद पात्र) में अभिकारक। (i) विलगित; (ii) खुला; (iii) बंद।
hi.sol: NCERT 5.1.2: खुला निकाय परिवेश के साथ ऊर्जा तथा द्रव्य दोनों का आदान-प्रदान करता है (खुला बीकर)। बंद निकाय ऊर्जा का आदान-प्रदान करता है पर द्रव्य का नहीं (कॉपर या स्टील का बंद पात्र)। विलगित निकाय न ऊर्जा का, न द्रव्य का आदान-प्रदान करता है (थर्मस फ्लास्क या कोई भी बंद ऊष्मारोधी पात्र)।
hi.hint: द्रव्य + ऊर्जा → खुला; केवल ऊर्जा → बंद; कुछ नहीं → विलगित।

questions.q: A cup of hot tea kept on a table (without lid) is an example of:
questions.sol: Vapour (matter) escapes and heat (energy) is lost, so both matter and energy are exchanged: an open system.

questions.q: Reactants sealed in a stoppered steel flask constitute a/an:
questions.sol: Matter cannot leave a sealed flask, but steel conducts heat, so energy can be exchanged: a closed system.

questions.q: For an isolated system, which is always true?
questions.sol: No heat or work crosses the boundary, so ΔU = q + w = 0. Entropy can still increase in a spontaneous change.

questions.q: Coffee kept in a perfectly sealed and insulated thermos flask is an example of:
questions.sol: Neither matter nor energy can cross the boundary.

questions.q: The state of a fixed amount of an ideal gas is completely described by specifying:
questions.sol: NCERT 5.1.3: in thermodynamics the state of a system is described by its measurable macroscopic properties: pressure (p), volume (V), temperature (T), amount (n) etc. These are state variables (state functions); their values depend only on the state, not on how it was reached. Describing positions and velocities of all molecules is not needed (and is impossible). For an ideal gas, fixing n and any two of p, V, T fixes the third through pV = nRT.
questions.hint: Macroscopic and measurable.
o: the position and velocity of every molecule
only the work done on it
measurable state variables such as pressure, volume and temperature (any two plus the amount, since pV = nRT links them)

hi.q: किसी आदर्श गैस की निश्चित मात्रा की अवस्था पूर्णतः बताई जाती है:
o: प्रत्येक अणु की स्थिति तथा वेग से
केवल उस पर किए गए कार्य से
दाब, आयतन तथा ताप जैसे मापने योग्य अवस्था चरों से (मात्रा के साथ कोई दो, क्योंकि pV = nRT उन्हें जोड़ता है)
hi.sol: NCERT 5.1.3: ऊष्मागतिकी में निकाय की अवस्था उसके मापने योग्य स्थूल गुणों से बताई जाती है: दाब (p), आयतन (V), ताप (T), मात्रा (n) आदि। ये अवस्था चर (अवस्था फलन) हैं; इनके मान केवल अवस्था पर निर्भर करते हैं, उस तक पहुँचने के तरीके पर नहीं। सभी अणुओं की स्थिति और वेग बताना आवश्यक नहीं है (और असंभव है)। आदर्श गैस के लिए n तथा p, V, T में से कोई दो निश्चित करने पर तीसरा pV = nRT से निश्चित हो जाता है।
hi.hint: स्थूल और मापने योग्य।

questions.q: A thermodynamic state function is a quantity:
questions.sol: By definition, a state function depends only on the state of the system, not on how that state was reached.
o: Whose value is independent of path
Whose value depends on temperature only

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a state function?
questions.sol: Work depends on the path. U, H and S are state functions.

questions.q: Which combination is a state function?
questions.sol: q + w = ΔU, which is a state function even though q and w individually are not.

questions.q: For a fixed amount of an ideal gas, how many of p, V and T must be specified to fix its state?
questions.sol: pV = nRT links the three; fixing any two determines the third.

sections.title: 5.1.4 Internal Energy as a State Function

questions.q: Which statement about internal energy U is incorrect?
questions.sol: NCERT 5.1.4: internal energy U represents the total energy of the system (chemical, electrical, mechanical etc.). It changes when heat passes in or out, work is done on or by the system, or matter enters or leaves. U is a state function: ΔU = U2 − U1 depends only on the initial and final states, whatever the path; q and w separately are path dependent, but ΔU = q + w is not. In an adiabatic process (no heat exchange) ΔU = wad. Only ΔU can be measured, not the absolute value of U.
questions.hint: U is a state function.
o: It is the sum of chemical, electrical, mechanical and other energies of the system.
Like heat and work, it depends on the path by which the change is brought about.
Its absolute value cannot be measured, only the change ΔU.
For an adiabatic change, ΔU = w<sub>ad</sub>, the work done on the system.

hi.q: आंतरिक ऊर्जा U के बारे में कौन-सा कथन गलत है?
o: यह निकाय की रासायनिक, विद्युत्, यांत्रिक तथा अन्य ऊर्जाओं का योग है।
ऊष्मा और कार्य की तरह यह भी उस पथ पर निर्भर करती है जिससे परिवर्तन किया गया।
इसका निरपेक्ष मान नहीं मापा जा सकता, केवल परिवर्तन ΔU।
रुद्धोष्म परिवर्तन के लिए ΔU = w<sub>ad</sub>, निकाय पर किया गया कार्य।
hi.sol: NCERT 5.1.4: आंतरिक ऊर्जा U निकाय की कुल ऊर्जा (रासायनिक, विद्युत्, यांत्रिक आदि) दर्शाती है। यह तब बदलती है जब ऊष्मा अंदर या बाहर जाए, निकाय पर या निकाय द्वारा कार्य हो, या द्रव्य प्रवेश करे या निकले। U एक अवस्था फलन है: ΔU = U2 − U1 केवल प्रारंभिक तथा अंतिम अवस्थाओं पर निर्भर करता है, पथ कोई भी हो; q और w अलग-अलग पथ पर निर्भर करते हैं, पर ΔU = q + w नहीं। रुद्धोष्म प्रक्रम (ऊष्मा का आदान-प्रदान नहीं) में ΔU = wad। केवल ΔU मापा जा सकता है, U का निरपेक्ष मान नहीं।
hi.hint: U अवस्था फलन है।

questions.q: The internal energy of a closed system can change by:
questions.sol: In general U changes by heat, work or matter transfer. A closed system cannot exchange matter, so only heat and work remain.

questions.q: For a process to occur under adiabatic conditions, the correct condition is:
questions.sol: Adiabatic means no heat exchange with the surroundings, so q = 0.

questions.q: Joule's experiments with paddle-churning and electrical heating of water in an insulated vessel showed that:
questions.sol: Equal amounts of adiabatic work by different routes gave the same temperature rise, so U is a state function.
o: Mechanical work produces more heat than electrical work
A given amount of adiabatic work produces the same change of state regardless of how it is done
Internal energy depends on the path

questions.q: A system absorbs 701 J of heat and does 394 J of work. ΔU of the system is:
questions.sol: q = +701 J and w = −394 J (work done by the system). ΔU = 701 − 394 = +307 J.

questions.q: According to the IUPAC convention, work done on the system is:
questions.sol: Energy added to the system (work done on it) is positive.

questions.q: If no work is done on or by a system at constant volume, the change in internal energy equals:
questions.sol: With w = 0, ΔU = q.

questions.q: No work is done on a system but heat q is taken out of it. The system has:
questions.sol: Heat can leave only through thermally conducting walls. ΔU = −q (NCERT Problem 5.1 ii).

questions.q: The mathematical statement of the first law of thermodynamics (IUPAC convention) is:
questions.sol: With the IUPAC sign convention, ΔU = q + w.

questions.q: A gas does 200 J of work on the surroundings while 300 J of heat is removed from it. ΔU is:
questions.sol: w = −200 J and q = −300 J, so ΔU = −500 J.

questions.q: Which of the following can be measured absolutely for a system in a given state?
questions.sol: Volume has an absolute value. For U, H and G only changes can be measured.

questions.q: 2 mol of an ideal gas expands isothermally into vacuum (free expansion). The work done and the change in internal energy are:
questions.sol: NCERT 5.2.1: work against an external pressure is w = −pexΔV. In expansion into vacuum pex = 0, so w = 0 whether the process is reversible or not. For an ideal gas at constant temperature the internal energy does not change, ΔU = 0; with ΔU = q + w this also gives q = 0. So free isothermal expansion of an ideal gas: q = 0, w = 0, ΔU = 0.
questions.hint: Nothing to push against.

hi.q: 2 mol आदर्श गैस का निर्वात में समतापीय प्रसार (मुक्त प्रसार) होता है। किया गया कार्य तथा आंतरिक ऊर्जा में परिवर्तन हैं:
hi.sol: NCERT 5.2.1: बाह्य दाब के विरुद्ध कार्य w = −pexΔV है। निर्वात में प्रसार में pex = 0, अतः w = 0, प्रक्रम उत्क्रमणीय हो या नहीं। स्थिर ताप पर आदर्श गैस की आंतरिक ऊर्जा नहीं बदलती, ΔU = 0; ΔU = q + w से q = 0 भी मिलता है। अतः आदर्श गैस का मुक्त समतापीय प्रसार: q = 0, w = 0, ΔU = 0।
hi.hint: धकेलने के लिए कुछ नहीं है।

questions.q:
Under isothermal condition a gas at 300 K expands from 0.1 L to 0.25 L against a constant external pressure of 2 bar. The work done by the gas is :
[Given that 1 L bar = 100 J]
questions.sol: Work against constant external pressure: w = −pexΔV = −2 bar × (0.25 − 0.1) L = −0.3 L bar = −30 J. This is the work done on the gas; the work done by the gas is +30 J (NTA final key).
questions.hint: w = −p<sub>ex</sub>ΔV; the question asks for the work done by the gas.
questions.trap: −30 J is the work done on the gas (NCERT sign convention); the question asks for work done by the gas.

hi.q:
समतापीय परिस्थिति में 300 K पर एक गैस 2 bar के स्थिर बाह्य दाब के विरुद्ध 0.1 L से 0.25 L तक प्रसरित होती है। गैस द्वारा किया गया कार्य है :
[दिया है 1 L bar = 100 J]
hi.sol: स्थिर बाह्य दाब के विरुद्ध कार्य: w = −pexΔV = −2 bar × (0.25 − 0.1) L = −0.3 L bar = −30 J। यह गैस पर किया गया कार्य है; गैस द्वारा किया गया कार्य +30 J है (NTA अंतिम उत्तर कुंजी)।
hi.hint: w = −p<sub>ex</sub>ΔV; प्रश्न गैस द्वारा किया गया कार्य पूछता है।
hi.trap: −30 J गैस पर किया गया कार्य है (NCERT चिह्न परिपाटी); प्रश्न गैस द्वारा किया गया कार्य पूछता है।

questions.check: Matches the official key (NTA NEET 2019 final key, Code S2: 2)

questions.q: An ideal gas expands from 2 L to 5 L against a constant external pressure of 1 atm. The work done (1 L atm = 101.3 J) is about:
questions.sol: w = −p_ex ΔV = −1 × (5 − 2) = −3 L atm ≈ −304 J. It is negative because the gas does work on the surroundings.

questions.q: During compression of a gas, the sign of work (IUPAC) is positive because:
questions.sol: In compression V_f < V_i, so ΔV < 0 and w = −p_ex ΔV > 0.
o: ΔV is negative, and w = −p_ex ΔV

questions.q: A reversible process is one which:
questions.sol: NCERT: a reversible process proceeds infinitely slowly through equilibrium states and can be reversed by an infinitesimal change.
o: Proceeds infinitely slowly through a series of equilibrium states
Can be reversed only by a large change

questions.q: For the same initial and final volumes, the magnitude of work done BY a gas on isothermal expansion is maximum when the expansion is:
questions.sol: In reversible expansion, p_ex tracks the gas pressure, giving the largest area under the p–V curve.

questions.q:
The work done during reversible isothermal expansion of one mole of hydrogen gas at 25°C from pressure of 20 atmosphere to 10 atmosphere is
(Given R = 2.0 cal K−1 mol−1)
questions.sol:
For reversible isothermal expansion: w = −2.303 nRT log(p1/p2).

w = −2.303 × 1 × 2.0 × 298 × log(20/10) = −2.303 × 596 × 0.301 = −413.14 cal (negative: work is done by the gas).
questions.hint: Use p<sub>1</sub>/p<sub>2</sub> in place of V<sub>2</sub>/V<sub>1</sub> (Boyle's law).

hi.q:
25°C पर एक मोल हाइड्रोजन गैस के 20 वायुमंडल से 10 वायुमंडल दाब तक उत्क्रमणीय समतापीय प्रसरण में किया गया कार्य है
(दिया है R = 2.0 cal K−1 mol−1)
hi.hint: V<sub>2</sub>/V<sub>1</sub> के स्थान पर p<sub>1</sub>/p<sub>2</sub> लें (बॉयल का नियम)।

questions.q: 2 mol of an ideal gas expand isothermally and reversibly at 300 K from 10 L to 100 L. Work done is about (R = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹):
In the expression w_rev = −2.303 nRT log(V_f/V_i), the ratio V_f/V_i can be replaced (isothermal ideal gas) by:
questions.sol: Boyle's law: p_i V_i = p_f V_f, so V_f/V_i = p_i/p_f.

questions.q: The correct option for free expansion of an ideal gas under adiabatic condition is:
questions.sol: Adiabatic → q = 0. Free expansion is into vacuum (pex = 0) → w = 0. Then ΔU = 0, and for an ideal gas ΔT = 0 (NCERT §5.2.1, free expansion).
questions.hint: Expansion against zero pressure does no work.

hi.q: रुद्धोष्म परिस्थिति में एक आदर्श गैस के मुक्त प्रसरण के लिए सही विकल्प है:
hi.sol: रुद्धोष्म → q = 0। मुक्त प्रसरण निर्वात में होता है (pex = 0) → w = 0। तब ΔU = 0, और आदर्श गैस के लिए ΔT = 0 (NCERT §5.2.1, मुक्त प्रसरण)।
hi.hint: शून्य दाब के विरुद्ध प्रसरण में कोई कार्य नहीं होता।

questions.check: Matches the official key (NTA NEET 2020 final key, Code F3: 3)

questions.q: An ideal gas expands isothermally into vacuum. Which is correct?
questions.sol: Against zero external pressure, w = 0. For an ideal gas at constant T, ΔU = 0, so q = 0 too.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II.
List-I (Process): (A) Isothermal process (B) Isochoric process (C) Isobaric process (D) Adiabatic process
List-II (Conditions): (I) No heat exchange (II) Carried out at constant temperature (III) Carried out at constant volume (IV) Carried out at constant pressure
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:

questions.q: For the reaction N<sub>2</sub>(g) + 3H<sub>2</sub>(g) → 2NH<sub>3</sub>(g) at 298 K, the relation between ΔH and ΔU is (R = 8.314 J K<sup>−1</sup> mol<sup>−1</sup>):

questions.q: In a bomb calorimeter, the heat measured for a combustion reaction gives:
questions.sol: NCERT 5.3: in a bomb calorimeter the substance burns in pure O2 inside a sealed steel vessel (the bomb), immersed in water; the steel vessel is rigid, so the volume is constant and no work is done (w = 0). hi.q: बम कैलोरीमीटर में किसी दहन अभिक्रिया के लिए मापी गई ऊष्मा देती है:

ΔU, क्योंकि अभिक्रिया स्थिर आयतन पर होती है (कोई प्रसरण-कार्य नहीं)

questions.q: ΔcH of methane, graphite and H₂ are −890.3, −393.5 and −285.8 kJ mol⁻¹. ΔfH of CH₄(g) is:

questions.q: Using mean bond enthalpies (kJ mol<sup>−1</sup>): H–H = 435, Cl–Cl = 242, H–Cl = 431, Δ<sub>r</sub>H for H<sub>2</sub>(g) + Cl<sub>2</sub>(g) → 2HCl(g) is about:
questions.sol: NCERT 5.5 (c): in the gas phase, ΔrH = Σ bond enthalpies of reactants (bonds broken) − Σ bond enthalpies of products (bonds formed). Bonds broken: 435 + 242 = 677 kJ. Bonds formed: 2 × 431 = 862 kJ. ΔrH = 677 − 862 = −185 kJ. The reaction is exothermic because the bonds formed are stronger than those broken. The formula applies only to gaseous species.
questions.hint: Broken minus formed.

hi.q: माध्य आबंध एन्थैल्पियों (kJ mol<sup>−1</sup>) H–H = 435, Cl–Cl = 242, H–Cl = 431 का उपयोग करके H<sub>2</sub>(g) + Cl<sub>2</sub>(g) → 2HCl(g) के लिए Δ<sub>r</sub>H लगभग है:
hi.sol: NCERT 5.5 (c): गैस प्रावस्था में ΔrH = अभिकारकों की आबंध एन्थैल्पियों का योग (टूटे आबंध) − उत्पादों की आबंध एन्थैल्पियों का योग (बने आबंध)। टूटे आबंध: 435 + 242 = 677 kJ। बने आबंध: 2 × 431 = 862 kJ। ΔrH = 677 − 862 = −185 kJ। अभिक्रिया ऊष्माक्षेपी है क्योंकि बने आबंध टूटे आबंधों से प्रबल हैं। यह सूत्र केवल गैसीय स्पीशीज़ पर लागू होता है।
hi.hint: टूटे घटा बने।

questions.q: Which statement about spontaneous processes is correct?
questions.sol: NCERT 5.6: a spontaneous process is one that has the potential to proceed without the assistance of an external agency. It need not be fast: H2 + O2 at room temperature is spontaneous but extremely slow. It cannot reverse by itself, but it can be reversed with external help. Many exothermic reactions are spontaneous, but some endothermic ones are too (melting of ice above 0 °C, evaporation of water, dissolving NH4Cl in water), so enthalpy decrease alone cannot be the criterion; entropy must also be considered.
questions.hint: Ice melts above 0 °C although it absorbs heat.
o: Every exothermic reaction is spontaneous and every endothermic reaction is non-spontaneous.
A spontaneous process can never be reversed by any means.
A spontaneous process proceeds by itself without external help, but it may be very slow, and a decrease in enthalpy alone does not decide spontaneity.

questions.q:
Consider the following reaction :
2A(g) + B(g) → 2D(g)
ΔU⊖ = −10 kJ mol−1 and ΔS⊖ = −44 J K−1 at 298 K
Identify the correct option with ΔG⊖ for the reaction and spontaneity of the reaction at 298 K.
(Given : R = 8.31 J mol−1 K−1)
questions.hint: Convert ΔU to ΔH first (Δn<sub>g</sub> = −1), then ΔG = ΔH − TΔS.
questions.trap: Using ΔU directly in place of ΔH gives +3.11 kJ, which is not an option; forgetting the sign of Δn<sub>g</sub> gives −1.635 kJ.

hi.q:
निम्नलिखित अभिक्रिया पर विचार कीजिए :
2A(g) + B(g) → 2D(g)
298 K पर ΔU⊖ = −10 kJ mol−1 और ΔS⊖ = −44 J K−1
298 K पर अभिक्रिया के ΔG⊖ और अभिक्रिया की स्वतः प्रवर्तिता के लिए सही विकल्प पहचानिए।
(दिया है : R = 8.31 J mol−1 K−1)
hi.hint: पहले ΔU को ΔH में बदलें (Δn<sub>g</sub> = −1), फिर ΔG = ΔH − TΔS।
hi.trap: ΔH के स्थान पर सीधे ΔU लेने पर +3.11 kJ आता है, जो विकल्प नहीं है; Δn<sub>g</sub> का चिह्न भूलने पर −1.635 kJ आता है।

questions.q:
The standard heat of formation, in kcal/mol of Ba2+ is :
[Given : standard heat of formation of SO42− ion (aq) = −216 kcal/mol, standard heat of crystallisation of BaSO4(s) = −4.5 kcal/mol, standard heat of formation of BaSO4(s) = −349 kcal/mol]
questions.sol:
Crystallisation: Ba2+(aq) + SO42−(aq) → BaSO4(s); ΔH = −4.5 kcal/mol.

ΔfH(BaSO4) = ΔfH(Ba2+) + ΔfH(SO42−) + (−4.5)

−349 = x − 216 − 4.5 → x = −128.5 kcal/mol.
questions.hint: Write the crystallisation step and apply Hess's law.

questions.q: For irreversible expansion of an ideal gas under isothermal condition, the correct option is:
questions.sol:
For an ideal gas, U depends only on T; isothermal → ΔU = 0.

An irreversible (spontaneous) process increases the total entropy of system + surroundings: ΔStotal > 0, i.e. ≠ 0.
questions.hint: Ideal gas: U = f(T). Irreversible: ΔS<sub>total</sub> > 0.

questions.q: For a given reaction, ΔH = 35.5 kJ mol<sup>−1</sup> and ΔS = 83.6 J K<sup>−1</sup> mol<sup>−1</sup>. The reaction is spontaneous at : (Assume that ΔH and ΔS do not vary with temperature)
questions.sol:
Both ΔH and ΔS are positive, so ΔG = ΔH − TΔS becomes negative above T = ΔH/ΔS = 35500/83.6 = 424.6 K ≈ 425 K.

Spontaneous at T > 425 K.
questions.hint: Find the temperature where ΔG = 0; convert kJ to J.

hi.q: किसी दी गई अभिक्रिया के लिए ΔH = 35.5 kJ mol<sup>−1</sup> और ΔS = 83.6 J K<sup>−1</sup> mol<sup>−1</sup> है। अभिक्रिया स्वतः प्रवर्तित होगी : (मान लीजिए कि ΔH और ΔS ताप के साथ नहीं बदलते)
hi.sol:
ΔH और ΔS दोनों धनात्मक हैं, अतः ΔG = ΔH − TΔS, T = ΔH/ΔS = 35500/83.6 = 424.6 K ≈ 425 K से ऊपर ऋणात्मक हो जाता है।

T > 425 K पर स्वतः प्रवर्तित।
hi.hint: वह ताप ज्ञात करें जिस पर ΔG = 0; kJ को J में बदलें।

questions.q:
Hydrolysis of sucrose is given by the following reaction.
Sucrose + H2O ⇌ Glucose + Fructose
If the equilibrium constant (Kc) is 2 × 1013 at 300 K, the value of ΔrG° at the same temperature will be:
questions.sol:
ΔrG° = −RT ln K (NCERT Eq 5.23).

= −8.314 J mol−1 K−1 × 300 K × ln(2 × 1013) (large K → strongly negative ΔrG°).
questions.hint: ΔG° = −RT ln K; note the minus sign and the given K.

hi.q:
सुक्रोस का जल-अपघटन निम्नलिखित अभिक्रिया द्वारा दिया जाता है।
सुक्रोस + H2O ⇌ ग्लूकोस + फ्रक्टोस
यदि 300 K पर साम्य स्थिरांक (Kc) 2 × 1013 है, तो उसी ताप पर ΔrG° का मान होगा:
hi.sol:
ΔrG° = −RT ln K (NCERT Eq 5.23)।

= −8.314 J mol−1 K−1 × 300 K × ln(2 × 1013) (बड़ा K → अत्यधिक ऋणात्मक ΔrG°)।
hi.hint: ΔG° = −RT ln K; ऋण चिह्न और दिए गए K पर ध्यान दें।
